OPEN OPERATIONAL FRAMEWORK / COMMUNITY EDITION / v1.1.0

Give data a purpose.
Make trust practical.

Conflicting numbers, unclear ownership and access that nobody reviews. KDV turns data governance into everyday work: one responsible owner, a clear agreement and evidence for each shared data product.

WHO THIS IS FOR

Find a useful starting point.

Different roles meet around the same decision. Choose the question closest to your work.

◈

Business leaders

“Which number can we use to make this decision?”

Agree a purpose, an owner and an outcome.

01 ↗◎

Data leaders and stewards

“We have tools. How do we make governance work?”

Connect responsibilities, definitions and a first contract.

02 ↗⌘

Engineering and architecture

“How do we implement the rule without rebuilding everything?”

Choose reusable controls and explicit operating boundaries.

03 ↗◇

Privacy, risk and audit

“Who authorised this use, and where is the evidence?”

Follow purpose, decision, implementation and review.

04 ↗↗

Analysts and AI teams

“Can I trust this data and use it for this purpose?”

Read a product agreement before requesting access.

05 ↗＋

Consultants and contributors

“Can we adapt the method and improve it together?”

Reuse original knowledge and propose a reviewed change.

06 ↗

THE WHOLE MODEL

Four connected views. One operating practice.

01⬡

Common baseline

Ownership, agreement, classification, authorised access and auditability.

02≋

Five operating layers

Connect policy to responsibilities, decisions, controls and evidence.

03→

Four-stage lifecycle

Cultivate → Govern → Share → Activate. Review what each stage produces.

04⊞

Structure and decision rights

Separate domains, products and execution environments; name who decides.

BIO-INSPIRED BY DESIGN

Different roles.
A shared ecosystem.

Hives and beekeeping give us a language for cooperation, local responsibility and care for the whole. It is an organisational metaphor: people, decision rights and data products remain explicit.

ILLUSTRATIVE APPLICATIONS

Different contexts. The same operating questions.

01 / Enterprise

From conflicting sales reports to an agreed revenue product.

Finance and sales agree definitions, freshness, an accountable owner and a versioned contract.

Explore product agreements ↗
02 / Municipality

See emerging service pressure across disconnected systems.

Combine permitted indicators from sectoral departments, with clear freshness, coverage and boundaries, to support proactive municipal management.

Read the full worked example ↗
03 / Professional council

Prioritise inspections with traceable, current information.

Reconcile authorised internal and external sources. Keep analytical prioritisation separate from the evidence and human decision required for an individual case.

Read the full worked example ↗

Fictional scenarios. Outcomes and review periods are examples, not customer claims or delivery promises.

A common baseline. Local decisions.

Every shared product needs ownership, a contract, a classification, policy-based access and an audit trail. Each ecosystem adapts role names, approval routes, thresholds and review cadences around that minimum.

  • Named ownership
  • Versioned contract
  • Classification
  • Access by policy
  • Auditability
